title: AI Image Generation: Prompts That Actually Work
description:
Why most AI image prompts fail and the specific prompt structure that consistently produces usable results.

#AIArt #AIImages #PromptEngineering

scenes.narration: If your AI-generated images keep coming out generic or weird, it's almost always the prompt, not the model.

Most people type a noun and hope for the best, 'a mountain landscape.' That's not a prompt, that's a topic. A working prompt describes subject, style, lighting, and composition separately, so the model isn't guessing what you actually want to see.
Add a specific art style. 'Watercolor,' 'studio photography,' '3D render' each pushes the output in a completely different direction.

Lighting matters more than people expect. 'Golden hour,' 'dramatic side lighting,' 'soft overcast light' changes the entire mood of an image far more than adding extra descriptive adjectives to the subject itself does.
Composition words help too. 'Close-up,' 'wide shot,' 'from above' control framing the way a camera direction would.

And when a result is close but not right, don't start over, just describe what to change, the same way you'd direct a photographer, and regenerate from there. Most tools let you refine iteratively rather than rolling the dice on an entirely new prompt every time.
The gap between a mediocre AI image and a great one is almost always five extra words of specificity, not a different tool entirely.
Try rewriting your next prompt with subject, style, lighting, and composition as four separate pieces. Subscribe for more AI tool breakdowns.
